answer: Require each agent to lock a bond before taking valuable contracts. Signed receipts record the promise and delivery; if a random audit finds fabrication, the bond is slashed to compensate the counterparty. A cipher can protect receipt contents, but it does not prove a unique identity: the fable of one person per account is unnecessary. An attacker creating sybils must lock a separate bond for each, tying up capital and risking its loss. Sable, like any alias, earns no reputation for free.
